passages.text: A Psalm of Asaph.
passages.sermon:
Asaph wrote this psalm.
Asaph was a leader among the Levites.
He served as a musician in the temple.
This psalm is a song or poem.
It is meant for worship.

passages.text: The Mighty One, God the LORD, speaks and summons the earth from where the sun rises to where it sets.
passages.sermon:
Asaph wrote this psalm.
God is mighty.
God is the LORD.
God speaks.
God calls to the earth.
He calls from where the sun rises.
He calls to where the sun sets.
passages.original: מִזְמ֗וֹר לְאָ֫סָ֥ף אֵ֤ל׀ אֱ‍ֽלֹהִ֡ים יְֽהוָ֗ה דִּבֶּ֥ר וַיִּקְרָא־ אָ֑רֶץ מִמִּזְרַח־ שֶׁ֝֗מֶשׁ עַד־ מְבֹאֽוֹ׃

passages.text: From Zion, perfect in beauty, God shines forth.
passages.sermon: God is perfect in beauty.\r\nGod is in Zion.\r\nGod shines forth from Zion.

passages.text: Our God approaches and will not be silent! Consuming fire precedes Him, and a tempest rages around Him.
passages.sermon:
God is our God.
God comes near.
God does not stay silent.
Fire goes before God.
The fire consumes everything in its path.
A violent storm surrounds God.
passages.original: יָ֤בֹ֥א אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ וְֽאַל־ יֶ֫חֱרַ֥שׁ אֵשׁ־ לְפָנָ֥יו תֹּאכֵ֑ל וּ֝סְבִיבָ֗יו נִשְׂעֲרָ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: He summons the heavens above, and the earth, that He may judge His people: “Gather to Me My saints, who made a covenant with Me by sacrifice.”
passages.sermon:
God is Judge over His people.
God calls to the heavens above.
God calls to the earth.
God commands both to witness His judgment.
God says, “Gather My faithful ones to Me.”
These faithful ones made a covenant with God.
They made this covenant by offering a sacrifice.
passages.original: יִקְרָ֣א אֶל־ הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם מֵעָ֑ל וְאֶל־ הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ לָדִ֥ין עַמּֽוֹ׃ אִסְפוּ־ לִ֥י חֲסִידָ֑י כֹּרְתֵ֖י בְרִיתִ֣י עֲלֵי־ זָֽבַח׃

passages.text: And the heavens proclaim His righteousness, for God Himself is Judge. Selah “Hear, O My people, and I will speak, O Israel, and I will testify against you: I am God, your God.
passages.sermon:
God is Judge.
God is righteous.
The heavens proclaim God's righteousness.
God Himself judges all.
Selah.
God speaks to His people.
God calls Israel to listen.
God says, "Hear, My people."
God says, "I will speak to you, Israel."
God says, "I will testify against you."
God says, "I am God."
God says, "I am your God."
passages.original: וַיַּגִּ֣ידוּ שָׁמַ֣יִם צִדְק֑וֹ כִּֽי־ אֱלֹהִ֓ים׀ שֹׁפֵ֖ט ה֣וּא סֶֽלָה׃ שִׁמְעָ֤ה עַמִּ֨י׀ וַאֲדַבֵּ֗רָה יִ֭שְׂרָאֵל וְאָעִ֣ידָה בָּ֑ךְ אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֱלֹהֶ֣יךָ אָנֹֽכִי׃

passages.text: I do not rebuke you for your sacrifices, and your burnt offerings are ever before Me.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God is their Judge.
God says, “I do not rebuke you for your sacrifices.
Your burnt offerings are always before Me.”
passages.original: לֹ֣א עַל־ זְ֭בָחֶיךָ אוֹכִיחֶ֑ךָ וְעוֹלֹתֶ֖יךָ לְנֶגְדִּ֣י תָמִֽיד׃

passages.text: I have no need for a bull from your stall or goats from your pens, for every beast of the forest is Mine— the cattle on a thousand hills.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God is Judge.
God says, “I do not need a bull from your barn.
I do not need goats from your pens.
Every animal in the forest belongs to Me.
All the cattle on a thousand hills are Mine.”
passages.original: לֹא־ אֶקַּ֣ח מִבֵּיתְךָ֣ פָ֑ר מִ֝מִּכְלְאֹתֶ֗יךָ עַתּוּדִֽים׃ כִּי־ לִ֥י כָל־ חַיְתוֹ־ יָ֑עַר בְּ֝הֵמ֗וֹת בְּהַרְרֵי־ אָֽלֶף׃

passages.text: I know every bird in the mountains, and the creatures of the field are Mine.
passages.sermon: God speaks in this passage.\r\nGod knows every bird in the mountains.\r\nAll the creatures of the field belong to God.
passages.original: יָ֭דַעְתִּי כָּל־ ע֣וֹף הָרִ֑ים וְזִ֥יז שָׂ֝דַ֗י עִמָּדִֽי׃

passages.text: If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world is Mine, and the fullness thereof.
passages.sermon:
God speaks in this passage.
God owns everything in the world.
God does not need anything from people.
If God were hungry, He would not tell anyone.
God says, "The world belongs to Me."
Everything in the world is Mine."
passages.original: אִם־ אֶ֭רְעַב לֹא־ אֹ֣מַר לָ֑ךְ כִּי־ לִ֥י תֵ֝בֵ֗ל וּמְלֹאָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Do I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?
passages.sermon:
God speaks.
God asks a question.
God says, “Do I eat the flesh of bulls?
Do I drink the blood of goats?”
passages.original: הַֽ֭אוֹכַל בְּשַׂ֣ר אַבִּירִ֑ים וְדַ֖ם עַתּוּדִ֣ים אֶשְׁתֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Sacrifice a thank offering to God, and fulfill your vows to the Most High.
passages.sermon:
God is the Most High.
God deserves thanks.
Give a thank offering to God.
Keep your promises to God.
Fulfill your vows to the Most High.
passages.original: זְבַ֣ח לֵאלֹהִ֣ים תּוֹדָ֑ה וְשַׁלֵּ֖ם לְעֶלְי֣וֹן נְדָרֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Call upon Me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you will honor Me.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God says, "Call upon Me when you are in trouble.
I will deliver you.
You will honor Me."

passages.text: To the wicked, however, God says, “What right have you to recite My statutes and to bear My covenant on your lips?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the wicked.
God calls them wicked.
God asks them a question.
God says, “Why do you recite My statutes?
Why do you speak about My laws?
Why do you claim My covenant with your mouth?
You have no right to do this.”
passages.original: וְלָ֤רָשָׁ֨ע׀ אָ֘מַ֤ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים מַה־ לְּ֭ךָ לְסַפֵּ֣ר חֻקָּ֑י וַתִּשָּׂ֖א בְרִיתִ֣י עֲלֵי־ פִֽיךָ׃

passages.text: For you hate My instruction and cast My words behind you.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the wicked.
You hate My instruction.
You reject My discipline.
You throw My words away.
You do not listen to what I say.
You ignore My commands.
passages.original: וְ֭אַתָּה שָׂנֵ֣אתָ מוּסָ֑ר וַתַּשְׁלֵ֖ךְ דְּבָרַ֣י אַחֲרֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: When you see a thief, you befriend him, and throw in your lot with adulterers.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the wicked.
You see a thief.
You run with him.
You join adulterers.
You share with them.
passages.original: אִם־ רָאִ֣יתָ גַ֭נָּב וַתִּ֣רֶץ עִמּ֑וֹ וְעִ֖ם מְנָאֲפִ֣ים חֶלְקֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: You unleash your mouth for evil and unharness your tongue for deceit.
passages.sermon:
You speak evil words.
You use your mouth to do harm.
You let your tongue tell lies.
You use your tongue for deceit.
passages.original: פִּ֭יךָ שָׁלַ֣חְתָּ בְרָעָ֑ה וּ֝לְשׁוֹנְךָ֗ תַּצְמִ֥יד מִרְמָֽה׃

passages.text: You sit and malign your brother; you slander your own mother’s son.
passages.sermon:
You speak against your brother.
You slander your own mother's son.
You harm your family with your words.
You attack those closest to you.

passages.text: You have done these things, and I kept silent; you thought I was just like you. But now I rebuke you and accuse you to your face.
passages.sermon:
God sees your actions.
You have done these evil things.
I, God, remained silent.
You thought I was like you.
You believed I approved of your ways.
Now I rebuke you.
I confront you openly.
I accuse you to your face.
passages.original: אֵ֤לֶּה עָשִׂ֨יתָ׀ וְֽהֶחֱרַ֗שְׁתִּי דִּמִּ֗יתָ הֱֽיוֹת־ אֶֽהְיֶ֥ה כָמ֑וֹךָ אוֹכִיחֲךָ֖ וְאֶֽעֶרְכָ֣ה לְעֵינֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Now consider this, you who forget God, lest I tear you to pieces, with no one to rescue you: He who sacrifices a thank offering honors Me, and to him who rights his way, I will show the salvation of God.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to those who forget Him.
He warns them to pay attention.
He says, “Consider this carefully, you who forget God.
If you do not listen, I may tear you apart.
No one will be able to save you.”
God says, “Whoever offers a thank offering honors Me.
Whoever lives rightly, I will show him My salvation.”
passages.original: בִּֽינוּ־ נָ֣א זֹ֭את שֹׁכְחֵ֣י אֱל֑וֹהַּ פֶּן־ אֶ֝טְרֹ֗ף וְאֵ֣ין מַצִּֽיל׃ זֹבֵ֥חַ תּוֹדָ֗ה יְֽכַ֫בְּדָ֥נְנִי וְשָׂ֥ם דֶּ֑רֶךְ אַ֝רְאֶ֗נּוּ בְּיֵ֣שַׁע אֱלֹהִֽים׃
